title: GCD / UMCP: The First Seam-Chain Casepack: A Worked Case Showing Composed Continuity Across Multiple Welded Seams
object_of_study: Composed continuity across an ordered finite sequence of locally evaluated seams under one frozen chain-accounting contract.
main_question: When do individually admissible local welds compose into one admissible seam-chain rather than merely a sequence of local successes?

claim_layers.claim: A single welded seam proves that one local continuity claim reconciles under frozen seam accounting; it does not yet prove that continuity composes across a sequence of seams (source abstract).

The paper constructs a bounded five-state local episode with two candidate local seams, 0->2 and 2->4, and asks whether the composed transition 0->4 reconciles as one chain-level continuity claim; each local seam is evaluated under the same frozen seam-chain contract.
Central result: local welds are necessary for seam-chain continuity but not sufficient unless the chain-level ledger also closes — 'no chain residual closure, no composed continuity'.

Source-stated non-goals: no new domain closure, no resistant-corpus continuity claim, no governance procedure, no universalized local return-rate closure, no portable chain law, no extension or redefinition of Tier-1, no claim that local welds compose automatically.
The library places this as a diagnostic casepack with a handoff role: the source's 'What This Enables Next' names later burdens it does not absorb.

scope: One bounded five-state local episode with two candidate local seams (0->2, 2->4) and their composition (0->4), evaluated under one frozen seam-chain contract for finite return, ledger change, drift and curvature debits, return credit, residual, identity, and stance.
exclusions: Does not introduce a new Tier-1 structure.
Does not stage a new domain closure.
Does not claim a universal return-rate constant.
Does not claim that all local welds compose automatically.
preserved_meaning: A local weld and a seam-chain are different burdens; composed continuity requires both local seam validity and global chain reconciliation.
distortion_or_substitution_risk: Inferring chain continuity merely because every local transition looks acceptable or because multiple finite returns occurred.
next_burden: Source-stated ('What This Enables Next'): a small domain closure with welded transitions (declaring its domain adapter before applying local weld and chain accounting), a publication-infrastructure casepack using receipt chains, a repository implementation of seam-chain validation, and a failure taxonomy for chain composition. The paper enables these burdens but does not absorb them; no external-domain chain closure is claimed to have occurred.
